proposed_widenings.name: passive_class_feature family
proposed_widenings.justification: Evasion is a permanent, always-on modifier with no activation cost, no use-count resource, and no reset cadence. The only ClassFeatureMechanics family is 'activation', which requires all three. Encoding Evasion as 'activation' with kind=free cost + fixed 0 uses would falsify the feature's structure — it fires automatically on every matching incoming save_gate, not on player choice.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed...

proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureEffect: modify_save_outcome
proposed_widenings.justification: Evasion replaces the standard save_gate outcome branches (success=half, fail=full) with (success=0, fail=half) for a specific class of incoming effects (Dex half-damage saves targeting the feature owner). No existing ClassFeatureEffect variant — grant_extra_action or heal_hp — covers this shape. The v4 atom 'modify_roll_substitute' addresses die roll replacement, not outcome-branch remapping on an external save_gate.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail

proposed_widenings.name: Feature suppression condition gate (Incapacitated)
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature explicitly does not apply when the Incapacitated condition is present. This is a passive suppression predicate with no surface representation in the current ClassFeatureMechanics schema. The v4 atom 'suppress' exists but there is no surface type for attaching a condition-predicated suppression gate to a passive class feature.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You don't benefit from this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

notes: Primary gap is the missing 'passive' class feature family. ClassFeatureMechanics only has 'activation', which models player-triggered features with use-count resources. Evasion is always-on state that intercepts incoming save_gates — the correct family shape is closer to a persistent passive modifier. A secondary gap is the save-outcome-override effect shape: no ClassFeatureEffect variant or v4 atom precisely models 'when a matching incoming save_gate fires against this creature, upgrade its outcome branches'. The Incapacitated suppression gate is a tertiary gap common to many passive features.
